## ESPN

# Roger Federer announces retirement; 20-time Grand Slam champion will play Laver Cup as final tennis event

Copy Link

Roger Federer is retiring from professional tennis at age 41 after a series of knee operations, closing a career in which he won 20 Grand Slam titles, finished five seasons ranked No. 1 and helped create a golden era of men's tennis with rivals Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. [...] "I am 41 years old. I have played more than 1500 matches over 24 years. Tennis has treated me more generously than I ever would have dreamt, and now I must recognize when it is time to end my competitive career."

To my tennis family and beyond,  
  
With Love,  
Roger pic.twitter.com/1UISwK1NIN

Federer's 20 Grand Slam titles rank third all time among men's players behind only contemporaries Nadal (22) and Djokovic (21). [...] His serving, forehand, footwork and attacking style will all be remembered. Also unforgettable were his matches against younger rivals Nadal, 36, and Djokovic, 35, who both equaled, then surpassed, Federer's Slam total and are still winning titles at the sport's four biggest tournaments.

results.title: Tennis - Roger Federer: His life in retirement - and what comes next
results.content:
This was the year that Federer, who turned 41 in August, announced his official retirement from the sport, some 24 years after he played his first match on the ATP Tour.

He shared the news in the most modern of ways – via social media – but with a Federer twist: A letter to his tennis family and friends... and most importantly, his fans. [...] Federer does own an Olympic gold – in doubles. He and Swiss partner Stan Wawrinka triumphed at Beijing 2008. He, however, was never able to triumph in singles. He came closest on Centre Court at London 2012, but ran into a red-hot Murray, settling for silver.

Federer’s 310 weeks at the world No.1 ranking is second only to Djokovic, though his 237 consecutive weeks is a men’s record – and he is the oldest man (at 36 years, 320 days) to hold the No.1 ranking. [...] Earlier on court, Federer has grown emotional, too: “It’s been the perfect journey and I would do it all over again,” he said, before catching himself in tears.

A post shared by Laver Cup (@lavercup)

## The legacy Roger leaves behind

While Serena sits an at Open Era-record of 23 major titles won, Federer – long the leader in the men’s race – bows out behind both Nadal (22) and Djokovic (21) in what many have called a golden era of men’s tennis.

results.title: Roger Federer turns 45: Achievements, family and a new chapter
results.content:
Roger Federer turns 45 this Saturday, August 8, firmly established as one of the most beloved and respected figures in sports history. Four years after retiring, the Swiss icon remains a global role model, a leading ambassador for tennis, and a symbol of grace both on and off the court. These days, his life revolves around tribute events, occasional exhibition matches, personal ventures, appearances at the sport's biggest tournaments, and, above all, his family, the foundation of everything he [...] Federer announced his retirement at the 2022 Laver Cup in London, capping his career with a farewell that captivated fans around the world. His final match, played alongside Rafael Nadal, produced one of the defining images of modern sports. The two rivals sat side by side, holding hands and wiping away tears as they acknowledged the end of an extraordinary era. [...] Even in retirement, Federer remains a familiar presence at the sport's biggest tournaments and special events.© Visionhaus/Getty Images
